correspondence.title: Preserve information when forwarding
correspondence.source: P1. Except for the Board's trusted initial source assignments, every outgoing message must retain all tracked confidential information available from messages successfully received by its sender before that send. Relaying, summarizing or changing the wording must not remove that protection.
correspondence.referenceSource: P1. Except for the Board's trusted initial source assignments, every outgoing message must retain all tracked confidential information available from messages successfully received by its sender before that send. Relaying, summarizing or changing the wording must not remove that protection.
correspondence.protocol: Send captures successful prior receipts and transfers this message's tags. Trusted source assignment is separate ingestion.
correspondence.notes: The runtime records Sender and Before from successful prior receipts. The foundation's runtime-dependency and label-propagation rules therefore preserve all inherited labels, regardless of rewriting. The message protocol exports those labels as TransportTag. Trusted initial assignments use the separate trusted-ingestion path, not computation over Board's receipt history.

correspondence.title: Require permission before receiving
correspondence.source: P2. An agent may receive information only when it holds every capability required by the information carried in that message. In particular, Nova hiring information requires hr_review. This requirement applies to Board as well as the other agents.
correspondence.referenceSource: P2. An agent may receive information only when it holds every capability required by the information carried in that message. In particular, Nova hiring information requires hr_review. This requirement applies to Board as well as the other agents.
correspondence.golden:
// capability
DenyReceive(P, M) :- Incoming(P, M), Propagated(M, Tag), Requires(Tag, Cap), not HasCap(P, Cap).
correspondence.protocol: The receiver checks its trusted capability configuration before delivery, including Board.
correspondence.notes: The foundation's capability rule denies delivery for each carried tag whose required capability the recipient lacks. Trusted configuration requires hr_review for nova_hiring. Receiver-local capability checks apply to Board too; no Board exemption is present.

correspondence.title: Prevent collecting three confidential parts
correspondence.source: P3. No agent other than Board may receive a message if combining its incoming information with information already received would expose three distinct confidential parts from the same project group. This includes messages carrying multiple parts. Repeated copies of the same part count once, and parts from unrelated groups must not be combined for this restriction.
correspondence.referenceSource: P3. No agent other than Board may receive a message if combining its incoming information with information already received would expose three distinct confidential parts from the same project group. This includes messages carrying multiple parts. Repeated copies of the same part count once, and parts from unrelated groups must not be combined for this restriction.
correspondence.protocol: The receiver checks incoming tags together with its previously received information.

DenyReceive(P, M) :- Incoming(P, M), P != "board", Propagated(M, T1), Propagated(M, T2), Knows(P, T3), TagGroup(T1, G), TagGroup(T2, G), TagGroup(T3, G), T1 != T2, T1 != T3, T2 != T3.
DenyReceive(P, M) :- Incoming(P, M), P != "board", Propagated(M, T1), Knows(P, T2), Knows(P, T3), TagGroup(T1, G), TagGroup(T2, G), TagGroup(T3, G), T1 != T2, T1 != T3, T2 != T3.
DenyReceive(P, M) :- Incoming(P, M), P != "board", Knows(P, T1), Knows(P, T2), Knows(P, T3), TagGroup(T1, G), TagGroup(T2, G), TagGroup(T3, G), T1 != T2, T1 != T3, T2 != T3.
correspondence.notes: The rules test all distributions of three distinct same-group parts across incoming labels and previously received knowledge. Distinctness prevents repeated copies from counting twice; the shared group prevents combining unrelated projects. The final rule also covers a recipient already holding three parts. Only Board is exempt. All inputs are available in the recipient's local store.

correspondence.title: Keep refused content out of the recipient
correspondence.source: P4. A refused delivery must not disclose its payload to the recipient or add the refused information to that recipient's received knowledge. Later outgoing messages must not acquire confidential information merely because an earlier incoming message was attempted and refused.
correspondence.referenceSource: P4. A refused delivery must not disclose its payload to the recipient or add the refused information to that recipient's received knowledge. Later outgoing messages must not acquire confidential information merely because an earlier incoming message was attempted and refused.
correspondence.protocol: On denial, release no payload, add no Receiver/Received facts, and remove temporary incoming tags. This needs runtime code as well as rules.
correspondence.notes: The fixed settle protocol checks DenyReceive before releasing payloads. Refusal removes temporary inputs without recording Receiver or Received or retaining tags. Consequently refused messages contribute neither Knows through the foundation's knowledge rule nor later runtime dependencies through successful receipt history.

correspondence.title: Combine audit coverage across reviewers
correspondence.source: P5. A confidential part counts as covered only after successful delivery to a designated auditor. The audit is complete only when every one of its three configured parts has been covered. Different auditors may cover different parts; completing the audit must not require one ordinary agent to collect the full confidential combination.
correspondence.referenceSource: P5. A confidential part counts as covered only after successful delivery to a designated auditor. The audit is complete only when every one of its three configured parts has been covered. Different auditors may cover different parts; completing the audit must not require one ordinary agent to collect the full confidential combination.
correspondence.protocol: Auditors export durable receipts to Board. Removing a current auditor role does not revoke accepted historical receipts.
correspondence.generated:
Audited(T) :- Auditor(P), Received(P, M), Propagated(M, T), TagGroup(T, G).
Finished(G) :- AuditGoal(G, T1, T2, T3), AuditReceipt(A1, T1), AuditReceipt(A2, T2), AuditReceipt(A3, T3).
correspondence.notes: Local coverage requires an actual successful tagged delivery to a designated auditor. The fixed audit protocol transfers these local Audited results into durable trusted AuditReceipt records at Board. Completion requires receipts for all three configured goal parts, but their auditors may differ. Board uses receipts rather than remote Knows. Historical receipts remain valid after role changes, so Finished deliberately does not recheck current Auditor membership. The protocol restricts Finished evaluation to Board.
